title: iF Design Award 2027
entryFee: From €400 per entry (regular, until Sep 18, 2026); €500 after
prizeMoney: iF Design Award trophy, seal, and global publicity (no cash prize)
shortDescription: One of the world's most prestigious design competitions, open to product, packaging, communication, interior, and UX design.
longDescription: The iF Design Award has run since 1954 and is judged by an independent panel of international experts across disciplines including product, packaging, communication, interior, and UX/UI design. Winning entries receive the iF seal, are published in the iF design app and yearbook, and are exhibited at iF's design centers in Hamburg and Taipei.
submissionFormat: Online entry with product images/renders; physical sample may be requested for the jury round

title: James Dyson Award 2026
entryFee: Free
prizeMoney: £30,000 international winner; £5,000 per national winner
shortDescription: An international student and recent-graduate award for engineering and product design that solves a real problem.
longDescription: Open to current and recent university students in engineering and design, the James Dyson Award rewards inventions that solve genuine, everyday problems. National winners are shortlisted before an international panel including James Dyson selects the global winner. The award emphasizes prototyping and iteration over polish.
submissionFormat: 1–2 A3 boards, a short process video, and supporting sketches submitted online

title: German Design Award 2027
entryFee: Free to register; participation fee applies once nominated
prizeMoney: German Design Award trophy and international recognition (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A cross-disciplinary award from the German Design Council, judged this cycle with a focus on communication design.
longDescription: Presented by the German Design Council, the German Design Award recognizes outstanding design work across product, communication, and architecture disciplines. Entrants must first be nominated before submitting; nominated work is judged by an independent jury of design experts, with winners announced at the awards show in Frankfurt.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the nomination platform: visuals plus a written project description

title: MUSE Design Awards 2026 (Season 2)
entryFee: $219 regular entry + $30 annual administrative fee
prizeMoney: MUSE trophy and global publicity (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A New York-based multidisciplinary design award spanning architecture, product, packaging, and graphic design.
longDescription: The MUSE Design Awards evaluate entries across dozens of subcategories, from architectural design to packaging and conceptual work. Judging is handled by a panel of design, media, and marketing professionals, and results include tiered Platinum, Gold, and Silver recognition rather than a single winner per category.
submissionFormat: Digital submission: images, a written description, and category-specific supporting material

title: A' Design Award & Competition 2026–2027
entryFee: Free to register; nomination fee applies only if shortlisted
prizeMoney: Trophy, gala presentation, and international press coverage
shortDescription: One of the largest global design competitions, covering over 100 categories including digital products and UX/UI.
longDescription: A' Design Award and Competition accepts entries across an unusually broad set of categories, including interface, interaction, and digital product design. Registration and initial submission are free; a nomination fee is only charged for entries that advance past preliminary review. Winners are announced annually on World Design Day, April 15.
submissionFormat: Digital submission: images, technical drawings, and a written design statement

title: Architecture MasterPrize 2026
entryFee: Tiered entry fee by deadline (early / regular / final pricing)
prizeMoney: Trophy and global publication (no cash prize)
shortDescription: An international prize covering architectural design, interiors, landscape architecture, and architectural products.
longDescription: The Architecture MasterPrize invites built and unbuilt work from architects, interior designers, and landscape architects worldwide. Past editions have drawn entries from more than 70 countries. Winners are announced roughly a month after the final submission deadline and are featured in the organizer's annual publication.
submissionFormat: Digital submission: drawings, renders, photographs, and a project narrative

title: Interior Design Best of Year Awards 2026
organizer: SANDOW Design Group / Interior Design magazine
entryFee: From $285 (early bird) to $350 (late)
prizeMoney: Trophy and industry-wide recognition (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A long-running US interiors award covering completed projects and furniture/product design across many typologies.
longDescription: Interior Design's Best of Year Awards honor standout interiors and the products that furnish them, judged by a panel of practicing designers and editors. Categories span workplace, hospitality, residential, and healthcare interiors alongside furniture, lighting, and materials, with winners celebrated at an in-person ceremony.
submissionFormat: Digital submission: project or product photography, plans, and a written narrative

title: Bundespreis Ecodesign 2026
organizer: German Federal Ministry for the Environment / Umweltbundesamt
entryFee: Fee scales by company size; free for the student/newcomer (Nachwuchs) category
prizeMoney: Recognition award plus PR and communications support (no cash prize)
shortDescription: Germany's federal design award for products, services, and concepts with strong ecological performance.
longDescription: Presented by the German Federal Ministry for the Environment and the Umweltbundesamt, the Bundespreis Ecodesign recognizes companies, studios, and researchers whose work combines ecological responsibility with high design quality. A dedicated Nachwuchs (newcomer) category is open to students and graduates who finished their degree within the last year. This cycle's application window has closed; the entry remains listed for reference ahead of the next call.
submissionFormat: Online application with product/service documentation and ecological impact data

title: Green Product Award 2027
organizer: Green Product Award / Green Future Club
entryFee: Tiered entry fee (early bird / regular / final pricing)
prizeMoney: Trophy, certification seal, and audience award (no cash prize)
shortDescription: An international award for sustainable products and services across 14 categories, from architecture to mobility.
longDescription: The Green Product Award has recognized sustainable products and services since 2012, inviting companies and start-ups to submit work across categories spanning architecture, consumer goods, mobility, and new materials. Nominees are published for public audience voting ahead of the final jury decision, with the award ceremony held in Berlin.
submissionFormat: Online submission: product images, a sustainability data sheet, and a written description

title: International Design Awards (IDA) 2026
entryFee: ~$250 per entry (professionals); ~$80 per entry (students), with early discounts
prizeMoney: Gold, Silver, and Bronze recognition plus press coverage (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A long-running Los Angeles-based award spanning architecture, interior, product, fashion, and graphic design.
longDescription: The International Design Awards recognize both professionals and students across five core disciplines: architecture, interior, product, fashion, and graphic design. Entries must have been completed within the last five years. Winners are graded Gold, Silver, or Bronze within each category, with top honorees also considered for Designer of the Year and Emerging Designer of the Year.
submissionFormat: Digital submission: images, technical details, and a project statement

title: Green Good Design Award 2027
organizer: The Chicago Athenaeum: Museum of Architecture and Design
entryFee: €375 per entry (+€25 if paying by bank transfer); +€100 late fee
prizeMoney: Trophy, exhibition, and international recognition (no cash prize)
shortDescription: An international award for products, graphics, and organizations with strong ecological and sustainability credentials, presented by The Chicago Athenaeum.
longDescription: Part of the Good Design Award family administered by The Chicago Athenaeum and The European Centre for Architecture Art Design and Urban Studies, the Green Good Design Award recognizes work across six category groups: architecture, graphic design, organizations & people, product design, research & technology, and transportation. Winners are exhibited and published as part of the Good Design Awards program.
submissionFormat: Online submission: 4-6 project images (JPG/PNG, 300dpi) plus a written project description (max 500 words)

title: Communication Arts Typography Competition 2027
entryFee: From $40 per entry (varies by category); +$10 late fee after Sept 4, 2026; student discount available
prizeMoney: Publication in the Communication Arts Typography Annual (no cash prize)
shortDescription: One of the most prestigious competitions for typographic excellence, covering hand-lettering, calligraphy, and type design.
longDescription: Selected by a jury of distinguished designers and art directors, winning entries in the Communication Arts Typography Competition are published in the Typography Annual, included in the magazine's January/February issue and distributed worldwide. Entrants are notified within roughly two months of the deadline; entry fees vary by category with a discount for student submissions.
submissionFormat: Digital upload of high-resolution images or PDF documents showing the typographic work in context

title: European Product Design Award 2026
entryFee: €400 per entry (professional); students receive 50% off; 50% off each additional category when submitting the same design
prizeMoney: European Product Design Award Trophy for the European Product Designer of the Year and Discovery of the Year (student) titles; other winners receive certificates (no cash prize)
shortDescription: An international product design award from Farmani Group recognizing innovation across categories like automotive, consumer electronics, and eco design.
longDescription: The European Product Design Award (EPDA) is organized by Farmani Group, the same organization behind the International Design Awards and Architecture MasterPrize. The competition draws entries from more than 58 countries across categories spanning automotive, consumer electronics, food and beverage, and eco design, judged by a jury of more than 30 international design leaders. The 2026 awards ceremony takes place in Venice.
submissionFormat: Online submission: 6–10 project images (professional photography preferred) plus a written project description; a supporting PDF may also be uploaded. A physical product sample is not required.

title: Tokyo TDC 2027 Annual Awards
entryFee: From $35 per entry in early submission (categories 1-8) up to $110 in final submission for larger categories; student rates run $20–$70 depending on category and timing
prizeMoney: Grand Prize: ¥200,000; other Prize-winning works: ¥100,000 each
shortDescription: A prestigious international typography and graphic design competition from the Tokyo Type Directors Club, open to designers worldwide.
longDescription: Tokyo TDC is one of the most respected typography and graphic design competitions internationally, evaluating work across multiple categories including typography, logotypes, packaging, and moving type. Entrants need not be professional type directors—applicants just need to have served as the type director on the submitted work—and a discounted student rate is available. Prize winners are notified in early December 2026, with results published online in mid-December 2026; the formal award ceremony (where prize money and diplomas are presented) and the accompanying exhibition run May 27 – July 8, 2027 at Ginza Graphic Gallery in Tokyo.
submissionFormat: Digital submission via the Tokyo TDC entry platform; category-specific image counts or PDF page counts depending on entry type

title: UX Design Awards 2027
entryFee: New Talent: €70 per submission; Product & Concept: €320 per submission (plus VAT); Nomination Package (Product & Concept): €2,250
prizeMoney: Nomination title, certificate, and trophy plus a PR/press campaign (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A biannual German award recognizing user-driven digital and physical products, concepts, and student projects in UX design.
longDescription: The UX Design Awards, organized by IDZ Designpartner Berlin, evaluate submissions across three tracks: Product (market-ready or soon-to-launch offerings), Concept (startups, prototypes, and research projects), and New Talent (bachelor's and master's degree projects). Judging emphasizes user-driven design and meaningful problem-solving, with nominees notified in December 2026 and winners announced in March 2027.
submissionFormat: Digital submission: 4 product images (JPEG, 3000×2000–4000×3000px), a project description (max. 500 characters), company/logo materials, plus optional promotional video and an R&D documentation PDF (max. ~10 pages) for jury review.

title: Buildner's Unbuilt Award 2026
entryFee: €140 (professional/company) or €120 (student) single registration fee, plus 4.5% VAT; registration open Jul 10 – Sep 23, 2026
prizeMoney: €100,000 total: 3 category winners (Small/Medium/Large) €20,000 each, 15 honorable mentions €1,000 each, 3 student prizes €5,000 each, best presentation award €10,000
shortDescription: An open international architecture prize for unbuilt (conceptual) projects, judged across small, medium, and large project scales with a dedicated student prize track.
longDescription: Organized by Buildner (formerly Bee Breeders), an established architecture-competition platform, the Unbuilt Award recognizes conceptual and unrealized architecture, interior, landscape, and furniture projects. Now in its third edition, entrants compete in Small, Medium, and Large categories, each with a €20,000 top prize, alongside honorable mentions, dedicated student prizes, and a best-presentation award, for a combined €100,000 prize fund. The competition is open to anyone regardless of professional qualification, entering individually or in teams of up to four.
submissionFormat: One anonymous A2 landscape panel (max 10MB) with visuals and explanatory text in English; video and animation are not permitted

title: Communication Arts 2027 Illustration Competition
entryFee: Varies by category (published in the organizer's Category Fee schedule); student entries receive substantial discounts
prizeMoney: No cash prize — winners receive a personalized aluminum Award of Excellence, worldwide publication in the Illustration Annual, and printed certificates
shortDescription: A long-running global illustration competition from Communication Arts magazine; winners are published in the print and digital Illustration Annual.
longDescription: Open to illustrators worldwide, the Communication Arts Illustration Competition accepts any illustration first published or produced between January 2026 and January 2027 (AI text-to-image submissions are excluded). Winners receive a personalized aluminum Award of Excellence, worldwide publication in the Illustration Annual, and a feature on the Communication Arts website. Entry fees vary by category, with substantial discounts for student entrants.
submissionFormat: Digital images as RGB JPG (max 2MB) or motion/animation as MOV, MP4, MPG, or GIF (max 500MB), submitted through the online competition system

title: Green Concept Award 2027
organizer: Green Product Award / Green Future Club
entryFee: €450 (free for students and graduates within 6 months of graduation)
prizeMoney: No cash prize — finalists receive digital certificates, personalized jury feedback, an online project gallery profile, and rights to use finalist/winner seals
shortDescription: Sibling award to the Green Product Award for early-stage sustainable design concepts and prototypes, with free entry for students.
longDescription: The Green Concept Award, run by the Green Future Club alongside the established Green Product Award, recognizes sustainability-focused design concepts and prototypes across 14 categories. Applicants must provide verifiable sustainability evidence supported by documentation. Finalists receive digital certificates, personalized jury feedback, and an online profile in the project gallery; the awards ceremony takes place in Berlin.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the gp-award.com portal with supporting sustainability documentation

title: WIN Awards 2026
entryFee: £585 + VAT per entry
prizeMoney: No cash prize identified in available materials — winners are recognized at the WIN Awards ceremony and in press/industry coverage; specific trophy or certificate details were not published on the official site
shortDescription: Annual international awards recognizing outstanding interior design projects across residential, commercial, and public spaces, organized by World Interiors News.
longDescription: Now in its 14th year, the WIN Awards (World Interiors News Awards) celebrate innovative, visionary interior design work worldwide across 27 categories spanning residential, commercial, and public spaces. Entries are judged by an international jury of design professionals. The 2026 edition is open for submissions with a final deadline of August 6, 2026; winners are announced in November 2026 (exact date not yet published).
submissionFormat: Online submission via the WIN Awards portal (win-awards.evessiocloud.com): project details, design features, materials, and supporting images per category. Exact image/word-count specifications are provided in the site's downloadable Entry Kit.

title: London Design Awards 2026 (Season 2)
entryFee: $30 flat administrative fee plus $209–$249 per category entry, depending on submission period
prizeMoney: No cash prize — Design of the Year winners receive a complimentary limited-edition LITO trophy and certificate; Platinum/Gold/Silver winners may purchase additional trophies or customized certificates. All winners get marketing benefits (social media post, winner interview, profile page, press release template, winner badge); Platinum/Gold winners are also featured in the LDA online gallery and on IAA/Muse.World social channels.
shortDescription: International, multi-discipline design competition covering 12 categories including product, architecture, UX/UI, and communication design, run by International Awards Associate.
longDescription: The London Design Awards is organized by International Awards Associate (IAA), the same organization behind the MUSE Design Awards. Season 2 of the 2026 program spans 12 categories — including Product Design, Architectural Design, Interior Design, User Experience (UX) and User Interface (UI) Design, and Communication Design — and is open to designers, studios, and brands of all backgrounds. Season 2 entries are accepted in tiers through a Final Extension deadline of November 6, 2026, with results announced December 18, 2026.
submissionFormat: Fully online submission: a project synopsis of roughly 350 words, flattened JPEG/JPG images (under 4MB, ~1,200px wide, 300dpi, RGB), an optional supporting PDF brief, and video/audio submitted via a Vimeo/YouTube/Youku URL. Physical product samples are not required.

title: KOKUYO Design Award 2027
entryFee: Free
prizeMoney: Grand Prix (1 winner): ¥2,000,000 (~$13,000); Merit Award (3 winners): ¥500,000 (~$3,200) each; New Generation Award (up to 10 student winners): ¥30,000 (~$200) each. Amounts stated are after applicable Japanese tax withholding.
shortDescription: International product design competition from Japanese stationery and furniture maker KOKUYO, open worldwide with a dedicated student category, themed 'dialogue' for 2027.
longDescription: KOKUYO DESIGN AWARD is an international product design competition run by KOKUYO Co., Ltd., a major Japanese stationery, office furniture, and workspace-tools manufacturer. Entries are open worldwide to individuals, groups, and corporations for original, previously unpublished designs of stationery, furniture, or tools used in working, learning, and living. The 2027 edition is themed 'dialogue,' accepts entries free of charge, and includes a New Generation Award judged separately from all student submissions (elementary school through graduate level). Submissions opened July 24, 2026 and close at noon JST on October 7, 2026, with results announced March 13, 2027.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the KOKUYO Design Award entry portal: entrant registration plus design proposal materials (visuals and a written description) uploaded through the site's ENTRY pages. Detailed file-format specifications are provided within the entry portal itself.

title: AIA International Design Awards 2026
entryFee: $350 USD (AIA International members) / $475 USD (AIA US-chapter members); non-members must also purchase current-year AIA membership to enter
prizeMoney: No cash prize identified — winners receive AIA International Honor Award or Merit Award designation, recognition at the AIA International Conference (Cairo, November 2026) and the AIA Conference on Architecture and Design (Philadelphia, 2027), plus features on the AIA International website and in publications.
shortDescription: American Institute of Architects awards program honoring architecture, interior architecture, urban design, and unbuilt projects located outside the United States.
longDescription: The AIA International Design Awards, run by the American Institute of Architects' International chapter, recognize built and unbuilt work by AIA-affiliated architects on projects located anywhere outside the US and its territories. The 2026 program spans seven categories: Architecture, Interior Architecture, Urban Design, Unbuilt Projects, Firm Award, Sustainable Future Award (developed with Dow), and Inclusive Design Excellence Award. Non-AIA members may enter but must complete an AIA membership application as part of submission. The 2026 submission deadline is Friday, August 14, 2026 at 5:00pm Eastern US time, with winners celebrated at the AIA International Conference in Cairo on November 14, 2026.
submissionFormat: Primary jury-review submission is a PDF (max 20 pages, max 10MB) with at least 3 project photographs plus floor plans, site plans, elevations, and sections. Separate high-resolution (300dpi+) images are required for exhibition/publication if the entry is selected.

title: Red Dot Award: Product Design 2027
organizer: Red Dot GmbH & Co. KG (Design Zentrum Nordrhein Westfalen)
entryFee: Tiered entry fee by registration phase (early bird / standard / late submission); exact 2027 amounts not yet published
prizeMoney: Red Dot trophy, quality label license, and international publicity (no cash prize for the main Product Design award)
shortDescription: One of the world's most prestigious product design competitions, recognizing outstanding product design across industries worldwide.
submissionFormat: Online registration and entry via the My Red Dot portal, with a separate registration required for each entry
longDescription: The Red Dot Award: Product Design is one of the largest and most renowned design competitions in the world, run by Design Zentrum Nordrhein Westfalen. Registration for the 2027 edition opens 14 September 2026 and runs through the late submission deadline of 15 January 2027, in early bird, standard, and late-submission phases with increasing fees. The award is open to manufacturers and designers worldwide whose products are made using an industrial production process and launched on the market between 1 January 2025 and 1 July 2027. Entrants register and submit via the My Red Dot online portal, with a separate registration required for each entry. Winners are notified by email at the beginning of April 2027, and the Red Dot: Best of the Best trophies are awarded at a gala evening at the Aalto Theatre in Essen, Germany, on 13 July 2027.

title: American Architecture Awards 2027
organizer: The Chicago Athenaeum: Museum of Architecture and Design
entryFee: $395 USD per entry online (plus $50 fee for bank transfer; $100 late fee applies after the deadline)
prizeMoney: No cash prize — winners are exhibited internationally and published in the Metropolitan Arts Press catalog
shortDescription: Annual program from The Chicago Athenaeum honoring outstanding American architecture, landscape architecture, and urban planning projects.
submissionFormat: Online application via awardapplication.com: a 500-1000 word project description, 10-12 images (16:9 or 1:1, 300dpi, max 6MB each), and a single PDF (max 25MB) of floor plans, sections, and elevations
longDescription: The American Architecture Awards, presented by The Chicago Athenaeum: Museum of Architecture and Design, recognize commercial, corporate, institutional, healthcare, transportation, educational, and residential buildings as well as urban planning projects, across more than 32 categories including specialized areas like energy buildings and restoration work. Eligible submissions must be the work of American architects, landscape architects, or urban planners (including international firms with U.S. offices) for projects built or unbuilt in the U.S., or by U.S. firms working abroad, since 1 January 2025. The submission deadline for the 2027 edition is 1 February 2027. Winning projects are exhibited internationally and published in the Metropolitan Arts Press catalog.

title: Communication Arts 2027 Photography Competition
entryFee: Varies by category (published in the organizer's Category Fee schedule); $10 per-entry late fee for entries between March 12–26, 2027
prizeMoney: No cash prize — winners receive a personalized aluminum Award of Excellence, publication in the Communication Arts Photography Annual (print and digital), and a certificate
shortDescription: International photography competition from Communication Arts magazine, honoring outstanding work across advertising, editorial, and other categories.
submissionFormat: Online submission: digital images as JPG/RGB (max 2MB) or motion entries as MOV/MP4/MPG (max 500MB)
longDescription: The Communication Arts Photography Competition is an annual international competition recognizing excellence in advertising, book, editorial, institutional, self-promotion, motion/cinematography, and unpublished photography, plus a dedicated Student Work category. Any photograph first published or produced between March 2026 and March 2027 is eligible, with entries accepted from any country; AI-generated submissions are excluded. The deadline for the 2027 competition is 12 March 2027 (midnight Pacific Time), with late entries accepted until 26 March 2027 for a $10 per-entry surcharge. There is no cash prize; winners receive a personalized solid aluminum Award of Excellence, a certificate, and publication in the Communication Arts Photography Annual (print and digital) along with online exposure. Only accepted entrants are notified, within about two months of the final deadline.

title: DNA Paris Design Awards 2027
entryFee: €350 per entry (Architecture, Interior, Product); €100 per entry (Graphic); €75 per entry for students in any category, with 50% off each additional category; 20% early-bird discount until Dec 18, 2026, 10% extended early-bird until Feb 19, 2027; +10% late fee for entries between the May 7 regular deadline and the May 21, 2027 final deadline
prizeMoney: DNA Award trophy; main category winners are named 'DNA Designer of the Year' (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A Paris-based multidisciplinary design award spanning architecture, interior, landscape, product, and graphic design, open to both professionals and students.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the DNA Paris entry portal: project images and a written description, with category-specific supporting material
longDescription: The DNA Paris Design Awards recognize outstanding work across five main disciplines — architecture, interior design, landscape, product design, and graphic design — with separate, lower-cost entry tiers for student submissions. Entrants can apply for up to five sub-awards within their main category. Main category winners are named DNA Designer of the Year, and all winners are celebrated at an annual awards ceremony in Paris.

title: A' Sustainable Products, Projects and Green Design Award 2026
entryFee: Registration is free; a nomination fee applies once shortlisted and scales by entry edition (Digital / Vision / Classic / Pro); exact 2026 amounts not published on the fee calculator page found this session
prizeMoney: A' Design Prize package of PR, marketing, and publicity tools for professional-edition laureates, plus trophy and gala presentation (no cash prize)
shortDescription: A sustainability-focused track of the long-running A' Design Award, recognizing sustainable products, projects, and green design across a broad range of industries.
submissionFormat: Online submission via the A' Design Award competition platform: images, technical details, and a written design statement
longDescription: Run by the same organization behind the flagship A' Design Award & Competition, the A' Sustainable Products, Projects and Green Design Award evaluates entries spanning eco-friendly furniture, sustainable architecture and interiors, renewable energy projects, green industrial design, and dozens of related categories. Professional-edition laureates receive the A' Design Prize, a package of PR, marketing, and publicity tools, and are celebrated at the annual gala presentation.

title: SDGs Design International Awards 2026
organizer: SDGs Design International Awards Committee (Kyushu University, Japan & Dongseo University, Korea)
entryFee: Free (no entry fee stated across the official pages found this session)
prizeMoney: Gold Award: KRW 3,000,000 + certificate; Silver Award: KRW 2,000,000 + certificate; Bronze Award: KRW 1,000,000 + certificate; Honorable Mention and Special High School Award: e-certificate
shortDescription: A binational academic design competition from Kyushu University (Japan) and Dongseo University (Korea) for student ideas addressing the UN Sustainable Development Goals.
submissionFormat: Word or PDF application form submitted by email to the organizing committee, per the format specified in the official call for entries
longDescription: The SDGs Design International Awards invite university, graduate school, vocational, and high school students worldwide — including those outside design programs — to propose creative design solutions to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Entries fall under four themes: Resilient Cities and Communities, Sustainable Green Design and Climate Action, Blue Sustainability (Oceans and Water), and other related topics. The competition is jointly organized by the design faculties of Kyushu University and Dongseo University.

title: Pavilion Atlas 2026
entryFee: €140 (architects/professionals/companies) or €120 (students) single registration fee, payable in full or via 3 monthly installments; registration open through Sep 16, 2026
prizeMoney: €20,000 total: 1st €10,000, 2nd €5,000, 3rd €3,000, Student Award €1,000, Sustainability Award €1,000, plus 6 honorable mentions
shortDescription: An international conceptual pavilion design competition from Buildner and ArchDaily, open to architects, artists, and creatives of all backgrounds.
submissionFormat: Digital submission of a conceptual pavilion design and supporting narrative, submitted in English via the Buildner platform
longDescription: Pavilion Atlas, organized by Buildner in partnership with ArchDaily, invites entrants to design a conceptual pavilion for a country of their choice, conveying a spatial narrative about that place. Open to architects, artists, and creatives regardless of professional qualification, entries are judged with dedicated prizes for students and for sustainability-focused designs, alongside the main placings. All submissions must be in English.

title: Kingspan MICROHOME 2026
entryFee: €140 (professional/enthusiast) or €120 (student) single registration fee plus 4.5% VAT, payable in full or via installments; registration open through Sep 30, 2026
prizeMoney: €100,000 total prize fund: €55,000 in Buildner prizes (1st €30,000, 2nd €10,000, 3rd €5,000, plus Student and Sustainability Awards), plus a separate €30,000 Kingspan Award and three €5,000 Kingspan Compliments
shortDescription: A Buildner and Kingspan-sponsored international competition to design a sustainable, energy-efficient microhome under 25m², open to all backgrounds.
submissionFormat: Four A2 presentation panels (suggested, not mandatory) submitted in English via the Buildner platform
longDescription: Now in its 11th edition, Kingspan MICROHOME challenges architects, designers, and creative thinkers to develop a modular, self-sufficient, energy-efficient microhome with a maximum footprint of 25 square meters for a hypothetical young professional couple. The competition is open to entrants of any professional background and includes dedicated Buildner Student and Sustainability Awards alongside the main placings and the sponsor-funded Kingspan Award. All submissions must be in English.
